experiment: Repeat frozen import-closure falsification with Python interpreter-required package initializer edges

code.detail: All existing parent package __init__.py source modules are treated as interpreter-required dependencies of importing each dotted module; transitive AST imports of these initializers are traversed
code.scope: Python import semantics within pinned source package; not arbitrary runtime dynamism

qualifications: Only known initializer-based counterexamples were repaired; no claim of completeness against runtime plugin loading, dynamic imports, global registries, environment, or altered dependencies.
Zero missed observations in this finite set does not prove universal soundness.
Only 157/213 evaluations were assessable under frozen Python 3.13 behavioral oracles. The 56 unassessable historical revisions were not counted as successes.
Savings fraction is a counterfactual comparison of observed oracle subprocess execution time plus indexing overhead, excluding repository clone/checkout, and not a production performance guarantee.
One short oracle per repository provides modest absolute work to avoid; this is not representative of expensive verification suites.
Original, external third-party repositories were not mutated; adversarial commits remained disposable runner-local commits.
conclusion: Generated interpreter-mandated initialization edges remove all three prior false reuse decisions; greater soundness against these cases incurs a measurable verification cost and does not establish a general semantic closure.
